steps.text: Place chicken breasts between two sheets of heavy plastic on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound chicken breasts with the smooth side of a meat mallet to about ½-inch thickness. Cut flattened breasts into several large pieces.
Place flour, salt, and black pepper into a resealable plastic bag, add chicken pieces. Shake gently until chicken thoroughly coated with flour mixture.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease an 8x8-inch baking dish.

Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chicken; cook until golden brown on each side, about 5 minutes per side. Place in the prepared baking dish, leaving oil and butter in the skillet.
Add green onions, mushrooms, and garlic to the skillet; cook and stir until mushrooms release their liquid and start to brown, about 10 minutes. Spread mushroom mixture over chicken pieces.
Add apple juice, lemon juice, and sugar to the skillet; stir until sugar is dissolved and mixture comes to a boil. Pour sauce over chicken and mushroom mixture; cover dish
Bake in the preheated oven until sauce has reduced and chicken has absorbed the sauce, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Yummy Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This yummy chicken recipe starts with pan-fried chicken breasts and a tangy sauce made with apple juice, lemon juice, green onion, and fresh mushrooms.

review.reviewBody: This really is yummy chicken! We loved the addition of apple juice, its a great fall recipe. I served this with apple stuffing and steamed veggies.

As written, this dish is a little bland. I have made a similar recipe (with the very same name) for more than a decade. It originally was featured in "Winners- Best Of Bridge" cookbook. A few ingredients are missing in this posting that really will make this a fantastic dish: 1) Add 1/4 tsp of thyme to the flour for additional seasoning 2) Add 1/2 tsp of salt to the lemon juice, apple juice and sugar. DO NOT cook it before pouring over the chicken to bake- simply mix the 4 ingredients together, stir to dissolve and pour over the chicken. Much simpler! By adding salt and thyme, the dish really does become memorable.

The smell while it is cooking really heightens the anticipation and the flavour does not disappoint! This recipe is now on the "favourites" list. Next time I make it I will try roasting some Panko crumbs on it with a little Parmesan cheese. I used 4 Portobello Mushroom caps instead of the 1/2 cup the recipe called for. In this case more IS better!

Excellent. In the flour mix I add some Montreal Chicken seasoning for a little more flavor. And I added about a quarter cup of wine in with the apple juice. Cooked it for less time and it was very moist. Served it with roasted potatoes and a ceasar salad.

I made this last night and it was delicious! Even my picky eater said, "This is really good." Followed the recipe almost exactly. I used chicken tenders which was what I had in the freezer. I was probably a bit heavy on the mushrooms. I was out of green onions so used shallots. I had to use a slightly larger pan than 8 x 8 but not as big as 9 x 13. I used raw sugar instead of white sugar. Will be making this again and thinking that I will double the sauce at the end. Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!

I used pounded boneless skinless chicken thighs. I added paprika, Taragon , herbal poultry seasoning along with the salt and pepper. Also I used low sodium chicken broth along with the apple juice. When I served it too my family I added fresh pomegranate seeds. It gave it a great crunchy tang to it. My family loved it . My son and daughter-in -law and 2 yr old grandson loved it. I will make this again. It is a yummy recipe that you can definitely add what you want. I'm going to try pork chops next time. A great fall dinner!

Pretty good. I doubled the mushrooms, garlic, and green onions. Also doubled the sauce. Next time I think I will put in a tablespoon of flour after cooking the veggies and before liquid to thicken the sauce. Served over buttered d egg noodles and side of green beans.

Tip: Use boneless skinless thicken thighs instead.

This recipe comes from the Best of Bridge. If anyone else here is familiar with Best of Bridge recipes, you'll know they have hundreds of amazing delicious recipes, and this one is no different.

I make this often and it's easy, doesn't require a lot of ingredients and doesn't take very long to prepare either.

As tipped above, I HIGHLY recommend you make this with boneless skinless chicken thighs instead of chicken breasts. The difference is night and day.

Delicious! I wasn't sure what to expect because all of the ingredients were so simple, but this really was Yummy chicken. I made some changes based on what our tastes are. I used extra mushrooms, green onions and lots more garlic just because I really like all those things and also doubled the amount of sauce because my chicken breasts were really large and I tend to like lots of sauce. Also used apple cider because that's what I had on hand. Turned out so delicously moist and yummy. I think I will make this next time we have company over.

This dish was tasty, I changed a little, but not much. When I sauteed the mushrooms and garlic I added an extra clove just to taste it up a bit and I also added a splash of Jack Daniels. About ten minutes before the end of the cook i sprinkled some fresh mozzarella cheese on it.

Winner winner Chicken Dinner.
Simple and tasty we enjoyed this very much. served with fried potatoes, and stove top stuffing with apples and mushrooms thrown in. will make again.
So delicious! Double the veggies and sauce. I serve it with yellow rice
This chicken dish was very juicy and easy to make. In the future I would add more seasoning and maybe an additional vegetable.
Very delicious! I added onions and lemon juice as suggested in another review.
very good! served over buttered egg noodles.
I made this for my husband's birthday dinner. Everyone loved it. I will use more mushrooms next time. Thank you for great and easy recipe.
SO AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS! I think my favorite of the ones I have tried on here!
